# Player-facing immersion

- Prioritize immersion in this alchemist exploration game. Write player-facing text as part of its world, not as explanations of software or permissions.
- Say as little as necessary. Do not replace technical explanations with lengthy atmospheric explanations; prefer silence, visual cues and brief labels.
- Players should discover the game's purpose and mechanics themselves through exploration, experimentation and journals exchanged with other players. Preserve journals as a primary medium for sharing discoveries rather than having the UI explain them.
- Avoid references to servers, commits, editable/read-only modes, or technical inventory synchronization in ordinary gameplay UI. Keep such details in logs and developer documentation.
- Use names, authors and concise in-world actions to identify journals and items, not to explain their significance. Do not reveal hidden outcomes, rewards, recipes, objectives or solutions before players discover them.
- Do not add tutorials, hints, lore explanations or explicit instructions to communicate through journals unless specifically requested. Provide only the essential interaction affordances and necessary confirmation of destructive actions.
- Preserve clear feedback when an action fails; immersion must not hide errors or imply success.
- Maintain both Polish and English localization when changing player-facing text.
